Package io.webagent4j.workflow

Class WorkflowEngine

java.lang.Object
io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowEngine
public final class WorkflowEngine extends Object
Deterministic, single-lane executor for Workflow definitions.

WorkflowEngine itself is stateless and safe to reuse: execute(io.webagent4j.workflow.Workflow, io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowInputs) constructs a private, per-call session holding all mutable execution state (variables, discovered secrets, step results), mirroring how BrowserCrawler isolates one crawl's state per call. Two execute calls against the same Workflow - even concurrently - never share variable state, discovered secrets, or step results.

Execution model: strictly sequential and fail-fast. Every step runs, in definition order, on the exact thread that calls execute(io.webagent4j.workflow.Workflow, io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowInputs) - there is no ExecutorService, no CompletableFuture, and no parallelism anywhere in this engine, so a caller-owned resource an action factory closes over (an IPage, for example) is never touched from a different thread. The first step that fails stops execution immediately; every later step is recorded as WorkflowStepStatus.NOT_RUN. A failed action is never retried: WorkflowEngine adds no retry layer on top of the action layer's own safe resolution retries.

No workflow-wide timeout, no cancellation: this phase relies entirely on the timeout semantics of the underlying action/browser backend for any one step; there is no dishonest Java-side deadline wrapped around an otherwise-unbounded call (see docs/workflow.md#limitations).

Resource ownership: WorkflowEngine owns nothing a caller supplied - no browser, no page, no action backend - and never closes anything an IWorkflowActionFactory captures.

Runtime failure contract: a RuntimeException thrown from a supported extension hook - IWorkflowCondition.evaluate(io.webagent4j.workflow.IWorkflowVariables), IWorkflowCondition.describe(), an IWorkflowActionFactory, or IPreparedAction.execute() - is caught and converted into a structured WorkflowResult; it never escapes execute(io.webagent4j.workflow.Workflow, io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowInputs). IWorkflowCondition.referencedVariables() is a separate, definition-time-only contract validated by Workflow.Builder.build() - this engine never invokes it. A Throwable that is not a RuntimeException (a JVM Error) is never caught. Programmer misuse at definition-construction time (an invalid Workflow.Builder.build() call) still throws IllegalArgumentException directly, since that is a build-time contract violation, not a runtime execution outcome.

Condition-result finalization: a custom condition's describe() is called at most once, at evaluation time - it must be, since only the condition's own implementation can render its text - and the resulting raw text is kept internally, unredacted and unbounded, until the workflow terminates (see PendingStepResult/ PendingConditionResult), mirroring how WorkflowOutputs' safe previews are computed once at final-result time. A built-in condition (WorkflowConditions) instead defers its description's rendering itself to finalization time (see IDeferredConditionDescription), so no unbounded intermediate text is ever retained for such a condition - see docs/workflow.md#resource-bounded-diagnostics. Either way, a secret revealed by a later successful step still retroactively masks an earlier step's already-recorded SKIPPED/SUCCEEDED condition description before it is ever redacted or bounded, exactly like it already retroactively masks an earlier public output. A terminal WorkflowFailure's own message is redacted and bounded immediately when it is constructed, not deferred: once a step fails, no later step runs, so no later secret can ever be discovered.
